The CLI does not scan `$PATH` at startup. Resolution is lazy: when `os.Args[1]` doesn't match a built-in subcommand, the CLI calls `exec.LookPath("entire-" + os.Args[1])`. If a binary is found and executable, it runs before Cobra parses arguments.

Rules, in order:

1. **Built-ins win.** If the first argument matches a Cobra subcommand (or one of its aliases), the external command is never considered.
2. **Reserved names are skipped.** Names beginning with `agent-` are reserved for the [agent protocol](external-agent-protocol.md). The resolver refuses to invoke them as external commands.
3. **Path-traversal candidates are rejected.** Names containing `/` or `\` never resolve.
4. **Found-but-not-executable surfaces as a launch error.** If `entire-<name>` exists on `$PATH` but lacks the executable bit, the resolver reports `Failed to run plugin entire-<name>` with exit code 1, rather than falling through to Cobra's "unknown command" path.
5. **Missing Graph offers installation.** When `entire-graph` is absent, `entire graph <command>` asks `Install the entire-graph plugin?` with Yes selected by default. Accepting installs `graph` through the configured plugin index using the normal managed installer, then executes the installed binary with all remaining arguments unchanged. This also works for bare `entire graph` and `entire graph --help`. Installation output goes to stderr. Declining, cancelling, or failing installation exits nonzero without running the command. Non-interactive sessions receive an `entire plugin install graph` hint instead of a prompt. Other missing plugin names still fall through to Cobra.

### Managed install directory

Remote installs report index lookup, release metadata, download (including checksum verification), and installation progress on stderr. Styled terminals show a spinner; non-terminal and accessibility output prints plain status lines as each step starts. Progress stops before confirmations and results, including when installation fails. The same reporting applies when `entire graph` offers to install its missing plugin and when installing dependencies. Asset-name probes share one download status per release. Confirmations read from the controlling terminal and render to the supplied output writer (stderr for on-demand installs and dependency prompts), preserving piped plugin input and output. EOF declines installation; cancellation stops the prompt and preserves signal termination.

Users can drop binaries anywhere on `$PATH`, but a per-user managed directory is also automatically discovered:

- **Default:** `$XDG_DATA_HOME/entire/plugins/bin` (Linux/macOS) or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\entire\plugins\bin` (Windows).
- **Override:** `$ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR/bin`.

The CLI prepends this directory to `$PATH` at startup via `cli.PrependPluginBinDirToPATH()` so the existing `exec.LookPath` resolution finds managed installs without any special-casing. This is purely additive — the kubectl-style `$PATH` model is unchanged.

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/),

## [0.10.6] - 2026-09-07

### Added

- A Windows PowerShell installer, `scripts/install.ps1`, works under both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7: `irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex`. It resolves stable and nightly releases, verifies SHA-256 checksums, installs `entire.exe` and `git-remote-entire.exe`, and delegates to Scoop for stable installs when Scoop is on PATH. Update nudges now print that one-liner — naming the directory the running binary lives in, so the installer replaces it in place — instead of sending you to the GitHub releases page. Install detection is per-OS (brew and mise on unix, Scoop and mise on Windows) and honours relocated install roots ([#2152](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2152), [#2217](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2217))

### Changed

- Reworked `entire runner setup` flags and interaction flow. Interactive setup now asks whether to tailor runners or create generic defaults; `-y` selects tailoring, replacing the deprecated `--run`. `--print-prompt` preserves the previous default behavior, `--defaults-only` creates generic runners, and `--dry-run` previews tailoring without writing files. `--agent <name>` skips provider selection for this run without changing saved settings. Non-interactive use requires an explicit mode ([#2272](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2272), [#2306](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2306))

### Fixed

- `entire trail create` now runs pre-push hooks when pushing the trail branch, allowing existing checkpoints to sync through the normal push path. Hook output and prompts are streamed instead of buffered, so checkpoint sync failures and OPF prompts remain visible ([#2239](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2239))
- `entire trail` commands work against Entire-native repos. Trail resolution discarded the forge and looked up `<owner>/<repo>`, so a native `/et/<project>/<repo>` remote with a same-named legacy GitHub mirror — `entirehq/marvin` — returned the `/gh/` repo's trails. The `et` namespace is now preserved through resolution, native repos are addressed by repository ULID against their home cell, and `list`, `show`, `update`, `delete` and runner trail gathering all follow ([#2245](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2245))
- A named pipe where Entire expects a config file no longer hangs the process. `mkfifo .claude/settings.json` made `entire doctor` block in `openat` until SIGINT, because `open(2)` on a FIFO with no writer waits for one. Every no-follow read now refuses a non-regular leaf before opening it, which covers all nine agents, the plugin manifest, doctor's log readers and the settings loader ([#2308](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2308))
- `entire enable` no longer silently drops Vercel deployment blocking in a repo whose `vercel.json` is an absolute symlink into a monorepo's shared config. `os.Root` refuses an absolute link target unconditionally, even one landing inside the root, and the refusal is not "file not found" — so the check reported `path escapes from parent` and returned false ([#2290](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2290))
- A concurrent checkpoint write can no longer silently discard an OPF rewrite. The OPF paths used go-git's compare-and-swap, which does not take native Git's reference lock, so a native transaction landing afterwards overwrote the rewrite while both reported success. Ref updates now go through a native `git update-ref --stdin` transaction that holds the lock across the symbolic-ref check, with a bounded retry for transient lock contention and a terminal error for a genuine stale value ([#2211](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2211))
- Session and checkpoint file locks revalidate the locked file's inode after acquiring, and retry against the current file if the name has since been replaced ([#2273](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2273))
- `entire doctor` reports a regular file, FIFO, socket or device node where an agent directory belongs. It tested for a symlink and nothing else, so those came back clean while every hook install and `os.Root` open failed on them; a regular file at `.claude` was additionally reported as `NOT READABLE` with a permissions remedy that could not fix it. `.claude/agents/`, `.codex/agents` and `.gemini/agents` are also scanned now, and a worktree root that will not open is reported rather than passing silently ([#2220](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2220), [#2290](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2290))
- The repo docs embedded into the tailoring prompt `entire runner setup` sends to the model are truncated on a rune boundary. The cap is a byte budget applied to text described in characters, so a doc whose 6000th byte landed inside a multi-byte rune put invalid UTF-8 into the prompt. A file that is not UTF-8 to begin with keeps its own bytes rather than being reduced to a truncation marker ([#2307](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2307))

content.text:
Branch restored. Here's my review of **PR #2324 — "Install Graph on demand with visible plugin installation progress"** (head `270d17b5`; the Cursor summary in the body is one commit stale).

Overall: the shape is right and the reasoning quality is high — routing progress through the context rather than a global writer, sniffing the reader to stop huh's accessible scanner from turning EOF into "yes", and opening a separate TTY so the prompt doesn't eat piped plugin stdin are all correct calls, each with the right comment. `go build`, `GOOS=windows go vet`, `mise run lint` (0 issues) and the new tests all pass locally; CI is green and Gates fails only on "no approvals".

Two things I'd fix before merge.

## 1. On-demand install dead-ends when the plugin is already in the managed dir

`plugin_on_demand.go:44` passes `remoteInstallFlags{}`, so `force` is false. If `entire-graph` exists in the managed bin dir but `exec.LookPath` can't resolve it — a dangling symlink from the "typical local-dev install" whose source moved, or a `PluginBinDir()`/`PATH`-prepend failure — the on-demand branch fires, the user is prompted, accepts, and `installRepoAtTag`'s guard aborts. Reproduced with a dangling `entire-graph` symlink in the managed dir:

```
Install the entire-graph plugin? [Y/n]
Checking plugin index...
Finding latest plugin release...
Fetching plugin metadata for v0.4.0...
install plugin: plugin "graph" already installed at .../bin/entire-graph; use --force to replace
```

Exit 1, three network round-trips spent, and the plugin never runs. The trailing comment in `installMissingPlugin` ("Execute the managed entry directly, even if the managed directory could not be prepended to PATH at startup") describes exactly this case, but the `FindInstalledPlugin` call that would satisfy it only runs *after* the install. Hoisting it above the prompt fixes both: if the managed entry is there, return its path and skip the prompt entirely.

## 2. The prompt renders to a writer that need not be a terminal

`openPluginPromptInput` reads `/dev/tty`, but rendering goes to whatever writer the caller passed — stderr. `CanPromptInteractively()` probes `/dev/tty` and never looks at the writer, so `entire graph 2>/dev/null` (or `2>log`, or any wrapper capturing stderr — precisely the audience for "installation output goes to stderr") gets a prompt nobody can see. Measured, non-accessible mode, pty for input and a non-terminal writer:

```
bytes written to the TERMINAL: 0, contains question=false
bytes written to the REDIRECTED writer: 373, contains question=false
ENTER RESOLVED THE PROMPT: answer=true
```

Zero bytes to the terminal, the tty in raw mode, 373 bytes of escape sequences into the redirect, and one Enter authorizing a download-and-exec — with `defaultYes` the default. The material for the fix is already in hand and thrown away: `tea.OpenTTY()` returns the output handle, and `plugin_confirm.go:20-22` closes it (on Windows, where `CONOUT$` is a separate handle; on Unix it's the same `*os.File`, so the branch is a no-op there). Either render to that handle when the supplied writer isn't a terminal, or decline to prompt. Related: the confirm path writes ANSI to a non-terminal writer at all, which is what `interactive.ShouldStyle` exists to prevent — `startPluginStep` in the same PR gets this right.

## Worth a deliberate decision

**`main.go:83-85` changes exit-code semantics for every plugin, not just on-demand.** The gate is `ctx.Err() != nil && procsignal.Load() != nil` — true whenever any Ctrl+C landed during the process, regardless of how the plugin finished. The root-command path next to it gates on `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)`, i.e. the command actually failed *because* of cancellation. Since Ctrl+C goes to the whole foreground process group, a TUI plugin that treats it as "quit" and exits 0 now makes `entire graph` die from SIGINT (130). It does incidentally fix `runPlugin` returning `-1` → `os.Exit(-1)` → 255 for a signal-killed child, which is worth keeping — but the gate wants to be narrower: the interrupted install, or `ExitCode() == -1`, rather than "a signal happened."

## Smaller

- **`plugin.go:69`** — `"Running plugin with command: %s"` prints only on the install path, omits the command name, and is empty for bare `entire graph`. Reads as leftover debug output.
- **Progress is opt-in and one obvious caller isn't opted in.** Only `runRemoteInstall` calls `withPluginProgress`. `entire plugin upgrade` reaches `InstallPluginFromRepo` at `plugin_install_remote.go:311` with a bare context, so every `startPluginStep` on that path is a no-op — while the docs say "Remote installs report index lookup, release metadata, download … progress on stderr."
- **`plugin_group.go:742`** still sends `"Browse cancelled."` to stdout, right next to the prompt that moved to stderr.
- **Hardcoded `"graph"`** in `resolvePlugin` has no named constant, unlike its neighbours `selfUpdatePluginName` and `officialPlugins`. Separately: `graph` isn't in `officialPlugins`, so the plugin this PR exists to drive adoption of is the one whose invocations are never tracked — deliberate or not, worth saying which.
- **Docs placement.** The progress paragraph is wedged directly under `### Managed install directory`, so that section now opens with prose about progress reporting and its actual content starts in the second paragraph. It wants its own subsection.
- **`uiform/prompt_terminal_test.go` asserts the literal `"\x1b[4A\x1b[J"`.** That pins the exact row count of a huh form *and* ultraviolet's cursor arithmetic; a theme tweak or the next upstream bump breaks it with a message that says nothing about prompts. Asserting the question text is gone from the final frame would survive both.
- **No CHANGELOG entry** for a user-facing feature.
- **The ultraviolet bump deserves a sentence in the PR body.** It's not just the prompt-clearing fix: `20260811…` → `20260906…` also brings right-margin clipping, grapheme-cluster wrap handling, a drift-row model, relative-mode cursor-clamp changes, APC/DCS pass-through and an OSC 8 parse fix, from an unreleased pseudo-version — and it lands on every TUI in the CLI (`activity`, the pickers, `experts --tui`), not only this prompt.

Two claims in the PR body I'd correct: prompts moving off stdout isn't only about the on-demand path — `confirmInstallOrCancel` and the browse picker's confirmation moved too, which changes `entire plugin install <url>` output for existing users. And the "Medium Risk" note's worry about "only the `graph` name is special-cased" is the least of it; the PATH edge case it gestures at is finding 1 above, and it's reproducible rather than hypothetical.

The changes are in. Summary of what I implemented while the full gate finishes:

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| On-demand install dead-ends on an already-installed plugin | `plugin_on_demand.go` — `FindInstalledPlugin` moved *above* the prompt; the managed entry is executed, which is what the function's own return contract already promised |
| Prompt invisible when the writer isn't a terminal | `plugin_confirm.go` — the opener now hands back the TTY's output handle instead of closing it (`pluginPromptTerminal`), and rendering falls back to it when the supplied writer isn't a terminal |
| Signal gate discarded the plugin's exit code | `plugin.go` + `main.go` — new `ExitPluginSignalled`; the re-raise is gated on the plugin's own outcome, not on "a signal fired somewhere in this process". Also fixes the pre-existing `os.Exit(-1)` → 255 truncation |
| `"Running plugin with command: %s"` | Now `Running entire graph search hello` — names the command, non-empty for a bare invocation |
| `plugin upgrade` showed no progress | `plugin_group.go` — opts into `withPluginProgress`, so its `startPluginStep` calls stop being no-ops |
| Browse cancellation on stdout next to a stderr prompt | `plugin_group.go` — follows its prompt to stderr |
| Hardcoded `"graph"` | `onDemandInstallPluginName`, beside `selfUpdatePluginName` |
| Docs paragraph wedged under the wrong heading | New `### Install progress and confirmations` section; rule 5 documents the already-installed case and the signal exit |
| `"\x1b[4A\x1b[J"` literal | Count-agnostic regex, with a comment saying why the row count is left open |

Both real bugs got regression tests, and I verified they're genuinely red without the fixes:

```
--- FAIL: TestPluginConfirmationRendersOnTerminalWhenWriterIsRedirected
    prompt did not reach the terminal: ""
    prompt leaked into the redirected writer: "Install the entire-graph plugin? [Y/n] \n"
--- FAIL: TestMaybeRunPlugin_GraphInManagedDirIsRunNotReinstalled
    an already-installed plugin must not prompt for installation
```

Three things worth flagging:

**I retract the changelog finding.** `CHANGELOG.md` is written at release time here (`changelog 0.10.6` commits) — no feature PR in the last twelve merges touches it. Nothing to add.

**My fix exposed a test-isolation hole, which I also fixed.** `TestMaybeRunPlugin_MissingGraphNonInteractive` set `PATH` but not `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR`, and `pluginParentDir` reads `$ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR`/`$XDG_DATA_HOME`/`$HOME` directly rather than going through `userdirs` — so it isn't covered by the `testdirs` fallback. Once the managed dir is consulted before the prompt, that test reads the developer's *real* plugins.
